_comment: Two-layer: 'US' rows are the federal layer and apply everywhere. A state row with the same program_key REPLACES the federal row (e.g. Florida caps its nonrecurring reimbursement at $1,000, below the $2,000 federal ceiling). eligibility_json gates a program: special_needs / military.

detail: A one-time reimbursement for reasonable and necessary adoption fees, such as court costs, attorney fees, and other adoption-related expenses. The federal ceiling is $2,000; each state sets its own rate up to that amount.

A recurring monthly payment for a child eligible for federal adoption assistance, administered by the state and generally lasting until the child reaches the age of majority. The amount is negotiated per child, so no dollar range is published nationally.
A child eligible for federal adoption assistance is entitled to both a monthly subsidy and Medicaid.
The Department of Defense reimburses up to $2,000 per child, or up to $5,000 per year, for adoption expenses incurred by military families.

Florida pays $5,000 annually (or another amount agreed in writing between the adoptive parents and the department), on a monthly basis, for the support and maintenance of the child until the 18th birthday. The monthly payment may not exceed the foster care maintenance payment the child would otherwise have received.
Florida reimburses up to $1,000 in nonrecurring expenses: attorney fees, court costs, birth certificate fees, travel, agency fees, and physical examination fees.
Children receiving a monthly subsidy are eligible for health care through Medicaid until age 18; some children remain eligible until age 21.
Children adopted from Florida care are eligible for free tuition at any Florida state university, community college, or vocational school, up until age 28.

New York pays the foster care board rate. For agreements approved since September 1, 2023 that is 100% of the rate, whatever the family's income. For July 2026 – June 2027 the basic monthly rate runs $1,083.82 – $1,304.97 upstate and $1,245.79 – $1,490.34 in New York City, Nassau, Rockland, Suffolk, and Westchester, depending on the child's age. A child with a documented disability may qualify for the special ($2,338.46), exceptional ($3,544.56), or extraordinary ($4,312.59) rate. Payments can continue until age 21.

program_name: New York nonrecurring adoption expense reimbursement
detail: A one-time payment of up to $2,000 for reasonable and necessary adoption fees, court costs, and attorney fees. The agreement has to be signed before the adoption is finalized, and receipts are due within two years of finalization.

program_name: New York Medicaid or medical subsidy
detail: Adopted children may qualify for Medicaid or, if not eligible for it, a state-funded medical subsidy. Coverage continues to age 21 for children with a disability; for hard-to-place children it ends at 18 unless there is a determination of need.

program_name: New York Foster Youth College Success Initiative
detail: Children adopted from foster care after their 13th birthday qualify for funding toward undergraduate costs, including housing and meals, at SUNY, CUNY, and private colleges that host a HEOP program.
